sender.en: “Federal Civil Service Commission”, “Immigration”, “Army” or another agency recruiting

name.en: Fake government job recruitment: pay for forms, shortlisting or an appointment letter

how.en: A message or post says an agency such as the Civil Service Commission, Immigration, the Army or NNPC is recruiting, with a link to an unofficial portal. Applicants are asked for personal details and to pay for application forms, shortlisting, a “processing fee” or an appointment letter, often through an “agent” who claims to have connections. Official recruitment in Nigeria is free and runs only through the agency’s own portal.

text.en: A WhatsApp message or post announces recruitment into a government agency with a link.
The link is not the agency’s official portal and asks for your personal details.
You are asked to pay for forms, shortlisting, a medical or an appointment letter.
An “agent” says they can guarantee you a slot if you pay quickly.

2026 Federal Recruitment exercise is ongoing, 4,500 slots available. Apply through the portal below and pay the ₦7,500 form fee to be shortlisted. Our coordinator can also secure your appointment letter, send your CV on WhatsApp: [link]

en: pay for recruitment form government job
agent promised to secure appointment letter for money
federal civil service recruitment link on whatsapp
asked to pay shortlisting fee for job
processing fee for government job offer
recruitment portal not on official website
Any fee for forms, shortlisting, medicals or appointment letters.
Links that do not end in the agency’s official .gov.ng address.
An agent or “coordinator” who says they can influence the result.
Check the agency’s official website and verified social media pages to see if recruitment is open.
Never pay anyone for a government job or appointment letter.
Report fake portals and agents to the EFCC or the NPF-NCCC.
